evidence.role: controlled-definition demand; no official wording beyond the required registry definitions is copied

hints: For centre of gravity, say what point can represent all of the object's distributed weight.
For moment, name the two quantities multiplied and specify how the distance is measured from the stated point.

walkthrough.text: Treat the two terms separately so each definition is complete.
For centre of gravity, replace the distributed gravitational pulls by the whole weight acting through one point.
The centre of gravity is the point through which the whole weight of a body may be considered to act.
For moment, multiply force by distance, but qualify the distance as perpendicular from the chosen point to the force's line of action.
The moment of a force about a point is the product of the force and the perpendicular distance from the point to the line of action of the force.

ai_rubric.observable: States that centre of gravity is the point through which the whole weight of a body may be considered to act
States that moment is the product of force and distance
Specifies the perpendicular distance from the point to the force's line of action

evidence.role: centre-of-gravity representation demand; original context and options

hints: Separate the force's location from its direction.
Ask which point represents the whole distributed weight and recall the direction of weight near Earth's surface.

walkthrough.text: A non-uniform object does not necessarily have its centre of gravity at its geometric centre.
The distributed gravitational effect is replaced by the whole weight acting through the centre of gravity.
Weight acts vertically downward, so option B combines the correct point and direction.

ai_rubric.observable: Selects one vertical downward whole-weight force through the centre of gravity

evidence.role: one-force moment calculation pattern; original context and values

hints: The question already gives the force and the perpendicular distance.
Use moment = force x perpendicular distance and keep the product in N m.

walkthrough.text: Known quantities are F = 18 N and d_perp = 0.40 m.
Use M = Fd_perp.
The matching choice is B. The unit check also works because N multiplied by m gives N m.

ai_rubric.observable: Selects 7.2 N m from 18 N x 0.40 m

evidence.role: perpendicular-distance misconception derived from definition demand; original context and options

hints: Ignore the handle length until you have located the force's full line of action.
Find the shortest perpendicular distance from the pivot to that line.

walkthrough.text: Extend the force's line of action through the handle and pivot.
Because the pivot lies on this line, the shortest perpendicular distance from the pivot to it is zero.
M = Fd_perp = F x 0 = 0, so option A is correct even though the force is applied far from the pivot.

ai_rubric.observable: Recognises that a line of action through the pivot gives zero perpendicular distance and zero moment

evidence.role: direct one-force moment and sense demand; original handle context and values

hints: Write the force and the stated perpendicular distance before substituting.
For the sense, picture the right side of the handle moving downward around the pivot.

walkthrough.text: Known quantities are F = 32 N and d_perp = 0.28 m.
Use M = Fd_perp = 32 N x 0.28 m.
M = 8.96 N m, which is 9.0 N m to two significant figures.
A downward force on the right of the pivot moves that side downward, so the turning sense is clockwise.
Check: 32 x 0.28 is less than 32 x 0.30 = 9.6, so 8.96 N m is sensible.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses M = Fd_perp with 32 N and 0.28 m
Obtains 8.96 N m or 9.0 N m
States that the downward force on the right produces a clockwise moment

evidence.role: whole-weight representation combined with a one-force moment; original display-arm context and values

hints: Replace all the small gravitational pulls on the arm by one downward force at the marked centre of gravity.
Calculate that force with W = mg, then use the 0.42 m horizontal separation as the perpendicular distance.

walkthrough.text: Represent the distributed weight by one vertical downward arrow through the arm's centre of gravity.
Calculate the force: W = mg = 3.6 kg x 9.81 N kg^-1 = 35.316 N.
The arm is horizontal and the weight is vertical, so the 0.42 m centre-of-gravity separation is perpendicular to the weight's line of action.
M = Wd_perp = 35.316 N x 0.42 m = 14.83272 N m, which is 15 N m to two significant figures.
The downward weight is to the right of the pivot, so it produces a clockwise moment.
Check: using 35 N x 0.4 m gives about 14 N m, consistent with the calculated result.

ai_rubric.observable: Represents the arm's whole weight as one vertical downward force through its centre of gravity
Calculates the weight as 3.6 x 9.81 = 35.316 N
Calculates the moment as 35.316 x 0.42 = 14.8 N m or 15 N m
States that the weight to the right of the pivot produces a clockwise moment

evidence.role: perpendicular lever-arm geometry and chained one-force calculation; original solar-panel context and values

hints: Draw the panel's whole weight vertically downward through its centre of gravity.
The perpendicular distance to a vertical line of action is horizontal, so use the horizontal component of the 0.75 m sloping separation.

walkthrough.text: Replace the panel's distributed weight by one vertical downward force through its centre of gravity.
The 0.75 m distance along the panel is not perpendicular to vertical weight. The needed horizontal separation is d_perp = 0.75 m x cos 40 degrees = 0.5745 m.
M = Wd_perp = 78.48 N x 0.5745 m = 45.1 N m, which is 45 N m to two significant figures.
The downward force acts to the right of the hinge, so the moment is clockwise.
When the panel is vertical directly above the hinge, the weight's line of action passes through the hinge. Then d_perp = 0 and M = 0 N m.
Check: 0.5745 m is less than 0.75 m, so 45.1 N m is less than the upper estimate 78.48 x 0.75 = 58.86 N m.

ai_rubric.observable: Calculates the panel's weight as 8.0 x 9.81 = 78.48 N
Identifies the perpendicular distance as 0.75 cos 40 degrees = 0.5745 m
Calculates a moment of 45.1 N m or 45 N m
States that the angled panel's weight produces a clockwise moment
States that the vertical panel has zero moment because the weight's line of action passes through the hinge
